title: Atomic patch and rollback safety for VPC runtime upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build an automated, auditable VPC/private data-plane runtime upgrade flow that provides atomic patching semantics for tenant workloads, guarantees zero user-visible downtime for serving traffic, and supports deterministic rollback in <5 minutes. This ticket covers the Terraform/IaC module integration, health-gated staging, state warm-up (KV + prefix cache), connection draining, and an immutable artifact-based rollback mechanism for customer-managed private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module 'tf_private_runtime_rollout' provides inputs for image tag, upgrade strategy, canary percentage, health gates, and priming policy
Upgrades can be executed via a single CLI/API call and complete without 5xx errors for 99.9% of incoming requests across all tenants in a green path test
Rollback invoked automatically on sustained gate failure (defined as 3 consecutive health probe failures over 2 minutes) and terminates in a verified state within 5 minutes
Runbook covers operator steps for manual abort, investigation, and post-mortem artifacts
End-to-end e2e test harness (local and CI) exercising canary -> ring expansion -> rollback with synthetic traffic and real KV priming
Observability: per-tenant rollout dashboard, rollforward/rollback audit trail, token-level cost delta averaged during rollout window
implementation_notes: Use immutable container images and tag-based routing in the operator to ensure deterministic rollback
Introduce 'upgrade-stage' label on compute nodes so telemetry can be aggregated per-stage (canary, ring-1, ring-n)
Health gating combines probe pass rate, latency p95, and KV warm cache hit ratio. All three must meet thresholds to proceed
Terraform: expose a module output that generates a signed run id and S3-compatible location for priming artifacts
Priming: run a controlled 'prefix warm' job after canary comes online. Job verifies KV warm percent > 80% before expansion
Connection draining: graceful worker shutdown with token-aware handoff; increase Quiesce timeout to allow in-flight KV ops to finish
Rollback path: operator simultaneously reverts routing rules and reinstates previous image tag; ensure immutable snapshots of ephemeral state used for verification
Backward compatibility: maintain compatibility shim for kernel selection if rolling to older quantized binaries
test_plan: Unit: operator state machine unit tests covering transition and rollback paths (CI)
Integration: local multi-node cluster test that simulates primed and cold start tenants
Canary e2e: inject synthetic traffic at canary weight, validate health gates and KV warm metrics
Chaos: simulate disk pressure and network partition on ring nodes during canary to validate graceful fallback
Performance: run a 2-hour soak with latency/SLA collectors to assert no regression at p95/p99
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: KV warm on some tenants may be extremely cold causing extended rollback loops. Mitigation: cap expansion speed and allow manual bypass with explicit approval
Risk: Terraform drift between customer-managed resources and operator state. Mitigation: module writes a signed manifest and operator verifies before changes
Risk: Operator bug triggers partial routing correction. Mitigation: introduce read-only dry-run mode and a safety TTL-based auto-rollback
Risk: High priming traffic increases cost. Mitigation: configure priming throttle and sampling policy per-tenant
deployment_steps_summary: 1) Create signed run id via Terraform module and upload priming manifest
2) Kick off operator canary with new image tag and health gate thresholds
3) Run priming job against canary, validate KV warm percent and latency gates
4) If canary passes, expand ring by pre-configured increments, repeating priming and health checks
5) On gate failure, operator flips routing back to previous tag and triggers alerting + audit entry
6) Post-rollout verification and cost/latency report generation
